text: {"title":"Coffee Brewing Fundamentals for Home Baristas","subtitle":"For beginner home baristas who want to brew a balanced cup by weighing, adjusting grind and temperature, and tasting with confidence.","description":"This 30-minute beginner course teaches you how extraction works and how to recognise under-extracted and over-extracted coffee by taste. You will learn to separate strength from extraction, and to weigh coffee and water at a chosen brew ratio so every cup is repeatable. The course then shows how grind size and water temperature change the cup for espresso, pour-over, French press and light or dark roasts. You finish by tasting your results and changing one variable at a time to improve the next brew.","seoTitle":"Coffee Brewing Fundamentals for Home Baristas | Online Course","seoDescription":"Learn extraction, brew ratios, grind size and water temperature in this beginner home coffee course. Taste, diagnose and improve every cup.","faq":[{"question":"Who is this course for?","answer":"It is designed for home baristas at beginner level who want to brew better coffee at home and understand why their cups taste the way they do.","citations":[]},{"question":"Do I need special equipment?","answer":"A kitchen scale is recommended, because the course teaches you to weigh coffee and water rather than measure with spoons. A thermometer is helpful for water temperature, but the course also explains a way to rest boiled water without one. Grinding with a burr grinder is recommended for more even particles.","citations":["{{frg_4}}","{{frg_8}}","{{frg_7}}"]},{"question":"How long does the course take?","answer":"The course takes about 30 minutes in total, split into three 10-minute lessons, and each lesson ends with a short quiz. A final test is also included.","citations":[]},{"question":"What will I be able to do after completing it?","answer":"You will be able to identify under- and over-extracted coffee by taste, calculate coffee and water weights for a given ratio and dose, choose a grind size and water temperature for your method and roast, and adjust one variable to improve your next brew.","citations":["{{frg_2}}","{{frg_5}}","{{frg_13}}"]}]}
